When the imam says Amin all should say it, for whoever's Amin coincides with the angels' has his past sins forgiven.
Declaring Allah's oneness a hundred times, or Subhan Allah wa bihamdihi, brings great reward; angels seek those remembering Allah, whom He forgives, and 'La haula' is a treasure of Paradise.
Allah has ninety-nine Names, and whoever believes in their meanings and acts on them will enter Paradise; Allah is witr and loves the odd.
Ibn Mas'ud explained that he did not come out to preach every day because the Prophet preached to them at intervals so they would not be bored.
Many are cheated of health and free time; true life is the Hereafter's; live as a stranger; hope outruns one's term, while love of wealth and long life grows.
Mahmud recalls the Prophet spraying water on his face, and Utban relates that Allah forbids the Fire to whoever says 'La ilaha illallah' sincerely, seeking Allah's pleasure.
Allah says His only reward for a believer who stays patient when a dear one dies is Paradise.
The Prophet feared not his people's poverty but worldly wealth pouring in and their competing for it; wealth is sweet, a good helper if earned lawfully and spent rightly.
The best people are the Prophet's generation and those after them; later will come people who testify unasked, betray, break vows and grow fat.
Khabbab said companions who died took none of their reward in this world, while those after them gathered wealth they could spend only on building.
Uthman performed ablution as the Prophet did, who said such ablution followed by two rak'at in the mosque forgives past sins, but warned against being conceited about it.
The righteous will pass away one after another until worthless people remain, like husks of barley or bad dates.
Perish the slave of money and clothes; man would want a third valley of gold; true wealth is a content soul; the rich have little reward unless they give.
A poor Muslim is better than an earthful of nobles, most in Paradise are poor, and the Prophet's household and companions often went hungry, living on dates and water.
The deeds most loved are regular ones even if few; act moderately within your ability, for deeds alone admit none to Paradise, not even the Prophet, without Allah's mercy.
After leading the prayer, the Prophet said Paradise and Hell had been shown to him towards the mosque wall, the best and worst things he had ever seen.
Allah made mercy in a hundred parts, sending one to creation; knowing all His mercy, a disbeliever would not despair, and knowing His punishment, a believer would not feel safe.
Having given all he had to the Ansar, the Prophet said Allah makes content whoever refrains from begging and gives patience to the patient, the best gift of all.
The Prophet prayed until his feet swelled, and asked why, he replied by asking whether he should not be a thankful slave.
Seventy thousand of the Prophet's followers will enter Paradise without accounts: those who do not practise ruqya or see evil omens, and who trust in their Lord.
Idle talk and excessive questioning were forbidden; guarding tongue and private parts earns Paradise; speak good or keep silent, harm no neighbour, honour guests; one word can raise or ruin.
Allah will shade one who remembers Him with tears, and He forgave a man who, fearing Him, had his family burn his body and scatter his ashes.
The Prophet likened himself to a warner of an approaching army whom some believed and were saved, and to a man holding back moths rushing into a fire.
A Muslim is one from whose tongue and hands Muslims are safe, and an emigrant is one who abandons what Allah has forbidden.
The Prophet said that if they knew what he knows, they would laugh little and weep much.
The Fire is surrounded by desires and Paradise by disliked things, and each is nearer to a person than the strap of his shoe.
The truest verse a poet ever said is that everything except Allah is perishable.
Whoever looks at someone given more property and better appearance should also look at someone below him.
Allah writes an intended good deed as one, a done one tenfold to seven hundredfold, an evil done as one; Anas said sins now thought trivial were once deemed destructive.
A brave fighter the Prophet called one of the Fire's people killed himself; one may seem to do Paradise's or Hell's deeds, but results depend on the last deeds.
The best people strive in Allah's Cause or worship alone in a mountain pass sparing others harm; a Muslim will flee with his sheep to save his religion from afflictions.
When honesty is lost, await the Hour; honesty will leave hearts until the trustworthy are rare, and people are like camels, hardly one in a hundred fit to ride.
Whoever makes his good deeds heard or seen to win people's praise, Allah will expose his real intention.
Riding behind the Prophet, Mu'adh was told that Allah's right on His slaves is to be worshipped alone, and their right on Him is not to be punished.
When a bedouin's camel outran the Prophet's swift she-camel Al-Adba, he said Allah lowers whatever is raised high in this world.
Allah declares war on whoever is hostile to His pious worshipper, who draws near through obligations, then extra deeds, until loved, and Allah becomes his hearing, sight, hand and leg.
The Hour is as close to the Prophet's sending as two fingers; it comes after the sun rises in the west, so suddenly that bargains and meals go unfinished.
Whoever loves to meet Allah, Allah loves to meet him; the dying believer, given good news, longs for that meeting, while the disbeliever, told of torment, dreads it.
Shown his place in Paradise and given the choice, the dying Prophet wiped his face with water, said death has stupors, and chose the highest companions with his last words.
The bedouins' Hour meant their death; death relieves the believer, and others of the wicked; the dead keep only their deeds, see their destination daily, and must not be abused.
